about.title: About Pregnancy Calculator
about.description: The Pregnancy Calculator estimates due date, current pregnancy week, and major milestones based on last menstrual period or conception date. Pregnancy dating tools can help with timeline review, appointment planning, and trimester reference, but medical guidance should come from a qualified healthcare provider. The calculator provides a general pregnancy timeline for reference use.

howTo.title: How to Use the Pregnancy Calculator

steps.title: Enter Last Menstrual Period
steps.description: Input the first day of your last menstrual period (LMP) for due date estimation.

steps.title: Or Input Conception Date
steps.description: Alternatively, enter your estimated conception date if you know when conception occurred.

steps.title: View Due Date
steps.description: See your estimated due date calculated based on the standard 280-day pregnancy duration.

steps.title: Check Current Week
steps.description: View your current pregnancy week and trimester with detailed progression information.

steps.title: Track Milestones
steps.description: Monitor important pregnancy milestones and fetal development stages throughout your pregnancy.

steps.title: Plan Appointments
steps.description: Use the timeline to schedule prenatal appointments and important medical checkups.

faq.q: How should I interpret the due date calculation?
faq.a: Due dates are estimates, and many births occur before or after the estimated date. Early ultrasound dating may provide a different estimate, so use the calculator as a general timeline reference rather than a definitive prediction.

faq.q: What's the difference between gestational age and fetal age?
faq.a: Gestational age is calculated from the last menstrual period and is about 2 weeks longer than fetal age. Fetal age is calculated from conception. Healthcare providers typically use gestational age for pregnancy dating and milestone tracking.

faq.q: When do the trimesters begin and end?
faq.a: First trimester: weeks 1-12 (organ formation), Second trimester: weeks 13-27 (rapid growth), Third trimester: weeks 28-40 (final development and preparation for birth). Each trimester has distinct developmental milestones and medical considerations.

faq.q: Should I rely solely on this calculator for pregnancy planning?
faq.a: This calculator provides general estimates, but you should consult healthcare providers for dating, care decisions, and individualized guidance. Factors like irregular cycles, medical conditions, or conception timing can change the timeline.
